title: 2027 Market Predictions: Here’s What We’re Actually Doing
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Couch Investor hosts a long roundtable with Tanner and Neil (Motley Fool) on positioning for 2027 after the AI sell-off, around a Catrini article arguing capex growth — not capex itself — has peaked, so AI names' future cash flows must be discounted more heavily. Couch lands in the middle: he leans toward the Mag 7 and hyperscalers as the safer 2027 bet, preferring Meta — he expects 20%+ appreciation from about $630 and picks it over Micron every day — and Google and Amazon over the AI ‘bottleneck’ trades. He still holds Micron (about $800; bought near $70, sold some this year, the rest is house money) but will not add: the risk/reward is too binary, down 40% or up 100%, and he doubts the market will pay his $1,200+ price target. He sold his entire Rubrik position days earlier on valuation after a roughly 90% gain, and he holds Reddit (averages $130s–140s, down 30% after earnings) without buying the dip or selling, pending a verdict on the Google-search referral risk. He is still very bullish on Palantir, a core holding, and more excited to buy Zeta next year at $32, preferably 20–25% lower. He plans a public portfolio for January 2027, without the bottleneck trade as its bulk. Also discussed: Nvidia (his largest semiconductor position), Nebius (about $130–135), SoFi, Uber, Apple, AMD at $480, Marvell and Lumentum (takeover bids rumoured). No new GOOGL call: ‘rather own more Google’ is a relative lean, not a new buy.

calls.thesis: 2027 lean: picks Meta over Micron every day of the week - expects 20%+ stock appreciation next year from ~$630; ad business about to overtake Google revenue-wise, 3bn+ users, Muse an early success; free cash flow negative near-term on data-centre/GPU spend, expected to turn positive in about a year.
calls.base_case: Core ads keep compounding; AI improves targeting while Muse monetisation starts earlier than usual at Meta.
calls.bull_case: Muse becomes a real revenue line and Reality Labs losses shrink as promised, restoring free cash flow.
calls.bear_case: Costs grew ~70% vs revenue +30% last quarter; no cloud business to offset the AI spend, unlike Microsoft/Amazon/Google.
